content.title: About
content.content: Potato tots are small fried balls made from grated potato, breadcrumbs and seasonings. They are commonly served in fast‑food restaurants and casual dining as a side dish or snack. They feature a crispy golden crust and a soft, fluffy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato tots were created in the United States in the 1950s as an alternative to traditional French fries.
They are often made from leftover boiled potatoes, making them an economical dish.
Some restaurants serve tots with a cheddar‑bacon cheese sauce.
There are many flavor variations: cheese‑infused, herb‑seasoned, spicy pepper, and even sweet cinnamon versions.
In Japan, tiny tempura‑battered potato balls called “toto” are a popular street snack.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes contain vitamin C, an antioxidant that aids the immune system.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: Potato tots provide a quick source of carbohydrates, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Some dietary fiber
items.content: Grated potato retains a portion of fiber that helps digestion.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Potatoes provide iron, essential for blood formation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the breading and frying, tots are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Trans fats and saturated fats
items.content: Frying in certain oils can create trans fats; using high‑smoke‑point vegetable oils reduces this risk.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Tots are often salted; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve potato tots hot as a side to burgers, steaks, or as a standalone snack. They are perfect for dipping in ketchup, mayo, ranch, or cheese sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked tots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen tots keep for up to 2 months; fry them directly from frozen without fully thawing.
